fields.text: A Web-Based Physics and Circuits Laboratory Management System with AI Capabilities for NU Fairview

The Physics and Circuits Laboratory of NU Fairview supports laboratory activities that require coordinated access to rooms, equipment, and consumable supplies. Its operations include maintaining inventory, scheduling laboratory use, processing equipment borrowing and returns, tracking student accountability, and preparing activity reports. Keeping these records accurate and accessible is essential to supporting laboratory sessions and managing available resources.

The current process relies on handwritten request forms, borrower’s slips, and spreadsheet records maintained by the laboratory head. Reservations, inventory quantities, borrowing transactions, and clearance records are recorded separately, requiring repeated encoding and manual cross-checking. This arrangement makes it difficult to monitor available resources, identify scheduling conflicts, trace damaged or missing equipment, and provide timely updates to requesters.

The proposed Web-Based Physics and Circuits Laboratory Management System with AI Capabilities for NU Fairview brings these operations into one platform. It integrates inventory management, laboratory reservations and approvals, equipment issuance and returns, borrowing slip records, clearance tracking, daily task records, disposal logs, and end-of-term reporting. Access is assigned according to the responsibilities of Class Representatives, Faculty, the Dean, Head Laboratory, and Laboratory Staff, with staff access limited to their assigned laboratory.

The proposed system has two AI-related capabilities: an authenticated laboratory Q&A chatbot for Class Representatives and Faculty, and Inventory Forecasting for Head Laboratory under Inventory Management. The chatbot answers approved Circuits / Physics laboratory information, equipment information / availability and operating hours from authorized records; it does not submit, change or approve reservations. Inventory Forecasting estimates next-month consumable needs and possible reusable-equipment shortages from existing stock and actual usage history. Forecasts are recommendations, not guaranteed outcomes or automatic purchasing decisions. Regular dashboards, threshold-based low-stock alerts and end-term reports remain non-AI functions; AI-written report summaries and AI reservation actions remain excluded.

Process. Head Lab opens Inventory Management, selects Circuits or Physics, and requests the next-month forecast. The system retrieves D4 inventory, D5 issue/return history and D2 request/item references, then checks completeness and history coverage. Actual consumed quantities support consumable estimates; borrowing and return timing support concurrent reusable-equipment demand. Cancelled/rejected requests and merely requested quantities are not historical consumption. Returned reusable equipment is not consumed.

Results. Display item, laboratory, current usable stock, forecast month, estimated consumption or concurrent demand, suggested consumable restock quantity or possible equipment shortage, a short explanation, history period, and generation date. Keep current low-stock alerts separate from predicted shortages. If the relevant history is insufficient or unreliable, show “Insufficient history” and the known stock/threshold alerts rather than a zero or invented estimate. Missing equipment timing must not be replaced by total monthly borrowing counts.

Human review and limits. Head Lab reviews the recommendation against known upcoming activities and decides what to restock outside this workflow. Generating or refreshing a forecast never creates a purchase, changes stock, or approves a reservation. Forecast results are dynamic; no Forecast table is required. Consumption is aggregated from return outcomes once, not added again from inventory ledger entries. Initial usage-based estimates must be evaluated against actual subsequent usage; a historical-average baseline is not a trained AI model. The forecasting method, minimum reliable history and measured error must be validated before claiming production AI accuracy.

Through these integrated functions, the proposed system aims to reduce repeated encoding, improve record consistency, make laboratory information more accessible, and support accountability in the use of laboratory resources.
The system is developed under the Agile methodology, following the Scrum Framework. Agile was selected because the requirements of this project continued to change throughout requirements gathering.

This project spans three (3) terms, each term running thirteen and a half (13.5) weeks and corresponding to one subject and one release: MNTSDEV in the second year third term, MSYADD1 in the third year first term, and MCSPROJ in the third year second term.

Product Vision. The product vision was formed during MNTSDEV from the operational problems of the Physics and Circuits Laboratory and the Product Owner: paper borrower's slips and laboratory service request forms re-encoded by hand, a Google Sheet and several workbooks whose borrowing records are not linked to its inventory, room availability checked against a separate weekly grid for each room, approvals signed on paper and stored outside the workbook, and consumable quantities that cannot be established without a physical count.

Product Backlog and User Stories. From that vision the team wrote the objectives as user stories and organized them into the product backlog presented in Table 1: to digitalize inventory and equipment borrowing, to provide reservation with conflict detection, to replace paper-based clearance, to record approval through authenticated Faculty and Dean accounts and publish request status, to provide an authenticated laboratory Q&A chatbot, and to record waste disposal. The backlog is a living artifact and is refined continuously as consultation produces new information.

Sprint Planning. At the start of each sprint, the team will pull the backlog items it forecasts it can complete into sprint backlogs, and state a sprint goal. However, it may be adjusted if there is new information or miscalculations.
The Sprint. Sprints will run at a fixed length. However, the fixed length will be decided when the development phase starts.

Sprint Review and Sprint Retrospective. Each sprint closes with a sprint review, at which is demonstrated to the laboratory head and the backlog is adjusted in light of what he raises, and then a sprint retrospective, at which the team inspects how it worked during the sprint, its collaboration, its tools and its process, and commits to at least one improvement for the next sprint. The review inspects the product, while the retrospective inspects the process.
Product Backlog Refinement. Findings from the review and the retrospective return to the product backlog, which the Product Owner reorders before the next sprint planning.

Current Status. As of this submission the product vision, the product backlog, the requirements analysis, the system models and the prototype are complete or in revision, and construction has not begun. Every item in Table 1 therefore carries the status Not Started, and the fixed length of the sprint is left unassigned until the development phase starts.

The system authenticates Class Representatives, Faculty, the Dean, Head Laboratory, and laboratory-specific staff. Under the current manual process there is no system at all — a requester fills out a paper form and brings it to the laboratory in person. Every role signs in with a dedicated system account and a system-generated password: a Class Representative's username is their NU Student ID, and every other role's username is their NU Fairview email. The system verifies the credentials, establishes a session scoped to the user's role and, for Head Laboratory and Laboratory Staff, their assigned laboratory, and loads the dashboard for that role. Physics Laboratory Staff and Circuits Laboratory Staff never receive standing access to the other laboratory's data.

Figure 2 presents the system as one process at DFD Level 0. Its six external entities match the Use Case Diagram and each appears once. The Class Representative and Faculty exchange request, availability, status, history, question-and-answer, and Borrowing Slip data within their permitted workflows; only the Class Representative receives Clearance Status. The Dean remains approval-only. Head Laboratory exchanges account, inventory, equipment, clearance, schedule, usage, daily-task, disposal, and reporting data across both laboratories. Physics and Circuits Laboratory Staff exchange inventory, equipment, and disposal data only for their assigned laboratory; they do not send schedule, usage-log, clearance, or daily-task actions. These 46 boundary flows are preserved in the Level 1 DFD. Laboratory dashboards remain read-only views of existing records; their presentation arrows are intentionally omitted from these DFDs.

Figure 3 is the formal detailed reference: it decomposes the system into five primary processes and ten canonical data stores, retaining the individual boundary flows. Process 1.0 manages user access and controlled account issuance. Process 2.0 manages reservations, availability, approvals, status, and history. Process 3.0 answers authenticated laboratory questions. Process 4.0 manages inventory, equipment issuance and return, Borrowing Slip Records, disposal, and optional Head Lab inventory forecasting. Process 5.0 manages schedules, session usage, Head-Laboratory-controlled daily tasks and clearance, and end-term reporting. Only Head Laboratory sends Schedule Update, Usage Entry, Daily Task Entry, and Clearance Action. Laboratory Staff contribute inventory, issuance/return, and disposal records within their assigned laboratory. The 73 independent flows comprise 48 external exchanges and 25 store exchanges. Forecast Request and Inventory Forecast are Head Lab boundary exchanges; historical item references support dynamic forecasting. Dashboard presentation arrows are omitted without removing the dashboard feature. Head Laboratory appears last in the entity column.

Figures 4 to 8 decompose the five-process formal Level 1 model into five separate images. Each uses the same plain, print-oriented style as Level 1: uniform peer shapes, a vertical child-process column, independent noun-labelled arrows, and clear space beneath each label. Every Level 1 boundary flow is mapped to its child process; separate reads and writes may realize the same parent flow at different stages. Full names and parent-flow references remain available in the editable diagram. Borrowing Slip, Clearance, Daily Task, and Disposal Records remain distinct. Only Head Laboratory manages Daily Tasks, and Process 3.0 remains an informational Q&A chatbot.

DFD Levels 0–2 use the same concise data-flow labels for both requesting roles: On-Schedule Request and Out-of-Schedule Request. For Faculty, On-Schedule Request means the laboratory activity within the assigned class schedule; it needs no additional academic approval. For Class Representatives, the on-schedule non-laboratory request requires the selected class Faculty's approval. I. Project Overview

#

The Physics and Circuits Laboratory of NU Fairview supports laboratory activities that require coordinated access to rooms, equipment, and consumable supplies. Its operations include maintaining inventory, scheduling laboratory use, processing equipment borrowing and returns, tracking student accountability, and preparing activity reports. Keeping these records accurate and accessible is essential to supporting laboratory sessions and managing available resources.

The current process relies on handwritten request forms, borrower’s slips, and spreadsheet records maintained by the laboratory head. Reservations, inventory quantities, borrowing transactions, and clearance records are recorded separately, requiring repeated encoding and manual cross-checking. This arrangement makes it difficult to monitor available resources, identify scheduling conflicts, trace damaged or missing equipment, and provide timely updates to requesters.

The proposed Web-Based Physics and Circuits Laboratory Management System with AI Capabilities for NU Fairview brings these operations into one platform. It integrates inventory management, laboratory reservations and approvals, equipment issuance and returns, borrowing slip records, clearance tracking, daily task records, disposal logs, and end-of-term reporting. Access is assigned according to the responsibilities of Class Representatives, Faculty, the Dean, Head Laboratory, and Laboratory Staff, with staff access limited to their assigned laboratory.

The proposed system has two AI-related capabilities: an authenticated laboratory Q&A chatbot for Class Representatives and Faculty, and Inventory Forecasting for Head Laboratory under Inventory Management. The chatbot answers approved Circuits / Physics laboratory information, equipment information / availability and operating hours from authorized records; it does not submit, change or approve reservations. Inventory Forecasting estimates next-month consumable needs and possible reusable-equipment shortages from existing stock and actual usage history. Forecasts are recommendations, not guaranteed outcomes or automatic purchasing decisions. Regular dashboards, threshold-based low-stock alerts and end-term reports remain non-AI functions; AI-written report summaries and AI reservation actions remain excluded.

Inventory Forecasting — Head Laboratory

Process. Head Lab opens Inventory Management, selects Circuits or Physics, and requests the next-month forecast. The system retrieves D4 inventory, D5 issue/return history and D2 request/item references, then checks completeness and history coverage. Actual consumed quantities support consumable estimates; borrowing and return timing support concurrent reusable-equipment demand. Cancelled/rejected requests and merely requested quantities are not historical consumption. Returned reusable equipment is not consumed.

Results. Display item, laboratory, current usable stock, forecast month, estimated consumption or concurrent demand, suggested consumable restock quantity or possible equipment shortage, a short explanation, history period, and generation date. Keep current low-stock alerts separate from predicted shortages. If the relevant history is insufficient or unreliable, show “Insufficient history” and the known stock/threshold alerts rather than a zero or invented estimate. Missing equipment timing must not be replaced by total monthly borrowing counts.

Human review and limits. Head Lab reviews the recommendation against known upcoming activities and decides what to restock outside this workflow. Generating or refreshing a forecast never creates a purchase, changes stock, or approves a reservation. Forecast results are dynamic; no Forecast table is required. Consumption is aggregated from return outcomes once, not added again from inventory ledger entries. Initial usage-based estimates must be evaluated against actual subsequent usage; a historical-average baseline is not a trained AI model. The forecasting method, minimum reliable history and measured error must be validated before claiming production AI accuracy.

Through these integrated functions, the proposed system aims to reduce repeated encoding, improve record consistency, make laboratory information more accessible, and support accountability in the use of laboratory resources.

II. Methodology

#

The system is developed under the Agile methodology, following the Scrum Framework. Agile was selected because the requirements of this project continued to change throughout requirements gathering.

This project spans three (3) terms, each term running thirteen and a half (13.5) weeks and corresponding to one subject and one release: MNTSDEV in the second year third term, MSYADD1 in the third year first term, and MCSPROJ in the third year second term.

Product Vision. The product vision was formed during MNTSDEV from the operational problems of the Physics and Circuits Laboratory and the Product Owner: paper borrower's slips and laboratory service request forms re-encoded by hand, a Google Sheet and several workbooks whose borrowing records are not linked to its inventory, room availability checked against a separate weekly grid for each room, approvals signed on paper and stored outside the workbook, and consumable quantities that cannot be established without a physical count.

Product Backlog and User Stories. From that vision the team wrote the objectives as user stories and organized them into the product backlog presented in Table 1: to digitalize inventory and equipment borrowing, to provide reservation with conflict detection, to replace paper-based clearance, to record approval through authenticated Faculty and Dean accounts and publish request status, to provide an authenticated laboratory Q&A chatbot, and to record waste disposal. The backlog is a living artifact and is refined continuously as consultation produces new information.

Sprint Planning. At the start of each sprint, the team will pull the backlog items it forecasts it can complete into sprint backlogs, and state a sprint goal. However, it may be adjusted if there is new information or miscalculations.

The Sprint. Sprints will run at a fixed length. However, the fixed length will be decided when the development phase starts.

Sprint Review and Sprint Retrospective. Each sprint closes with a sprint review, at which is demonstrated to the laboratory head and the backlog is adjusted in light of what he raises, and then a sprint retrospective, at which the team inspects how it worked during the sprint, its collaboration, its tools and its process, and commits to at least one improvement for the next sprint. The review inspects the product, while the retrospective inspects the process.

Product Backlog Refinement. Findings from the review and the retrospective return to the product backlog, which the Product Owner reorders before the next sprint planning.

Current Status. As of this submission the product vision, the product backlog, the requirements analysis, the system models and the prototype are complete or in revision, and construction has not begun. Every item in Table 1 therefore carries the status Not Started, and the fixed length of the sprint is left unassigned until the development phase starts.

Validate the selection, validate selected class members for Group or exactly one selected class student for Student Only, and persist GROUP or STUDENT_ONLY separately from Schedule Type. The submitting Class Rep and participating students are separate identities.
  • Includes: Select Resources / Equipment. Every completed submission requires resource selection. Display the selected laboratory catalogue, capture required items and quantities, and validate them against availability before submission.
Stakeholders
Stakeholder Interests
  • Class Representative: needs to submit an on-schedule non-laboratory request within the class's assigned schedule, or an out-of-schedule request, without a paper form.
  • Faculty: needs to request exceptional out-of-schedule use and review requests from the assigned Class Representative.
  • Dean: needs approval authority over out-of-schedule requests routed to the office, without being modeled as a requester.
  • Head Laboratory: needs requests to arrive complete and already scoped to the correct laboratory.
Conditions
Preconditions
  • The requester is signed in and has chosen a laboratory.
  • The laboratory schedule for the term has been recorded.
Postconditions
  • The request is stored as Pending and the selected block is held. Class Representative requests go to assigned Faculty first; out-of-schedule requests proceed to Dean only after Faculty approval. Faculty out-of-schedule requests go directly to Dean. This use case does not submit scheduled Faculty laboratory activities.
Flow of Activities
ActorSystem
  1. Requester chooses an authorized active subject/class, the laboratory and the intended block. The same section representative account is reused for different subjects.
  2. Requester selects required resources and quantities.
  3. Class Representative selects On-Schedule Non-Laboratory or Out-of-Schedule; Faculty selects Out-of-Schedule.
  4. For an on-schedule non-laboratory request, Class Representative confirms the assigned class block and states the academic purpose.
  5. For either Class Representative schedule variant, select the required Reservation Type: As a Group or As a Student Only. No option is preselected.
  6. As a Group: select participating students from the assigned class. As a Student Only: select exactly one existing student from that class; the representative may select a classmate or themselves. No individual student is preselected.
  7. Requester reviews the information and submits.
  1. System enforces the signed-in requester's allowed schedule variant and requires a valid Reservation Type for Class Representatives. Missing or invalid type prevents submission without creating a record or hold.
  2. System validates the selected class against the representative's active assignments and derives the reviewer from that class's Faculty. Reject an unassigned class; never trust a submitted Faculty ID or use the credential recipient as a global reviewer. GROUP retains members of the selected class; STUDENT_ONLY validates and records exactly one selected class student, not automatically the submitting representative, and ignores stale group-member input. Reject missing or out-of-class student selections. Keep requester_id as the submitting Class Rep account.
  3. System performs Select Resources / Equipment and validates item quantities.
  4. System validates an on-schedule non-laboratory block against the Class Representative's class schedule, or validates an out-of-schedule block as vacant.
  5. System stores reservation_type (GROUP or STUDENT_ONLY) with each Class Representative request, independently of request_basis / usage_type. Store Pending and hold the block: route Class Representative requests to assigned Faculty; route Faculty out-of-schedule requests directly to Dean.
Exception Conditions
Exceptions
  • If the selected slot is already committed, the system reports the conflict and offers the remaining vacant blocks.
  • If a requested resource quantity exceeds availability, the system flags it so the requester can adjust it.
  • If required information is incomplete, including Reservation Type and the applicable selected class students for a Class Representative, the system requests corrections before submission. Neither a reservation nor a hold is created.
  • If a Class Representative identifies the request as the class's scheduled laboratory activity, the system blocks that type and directs the class to its Faculty member.
  • If a Class Representative selects On-Schedule but the block is outside the class's assigned schedule, the system requires the request to be filed as Out-of-Schedule.

  1. Head Laboratory opens the broken or lost outcome and its borrowing slip record.
  2. Head Laboratory identifies and selects the responsible student from the reservation-linked borrowing participants: a selected group member or the selected Student Only borrower.
  3. Head Laboratory raises the clearance stating the item, quantity, and reason.
  4. Head Laboratory marks the clearance cleared or replaced on settlement.
  1. System displays the selected participants recorded on the reservation-linked borrowing slip and the damaged or missing item. Require Head Laboratory to identify the responsible student before creating clearance.
  2. System writes the clearance against the identified student and makes the student name, item, reason and status visible in the section Class Rep account. The Class Rep can view the record but cannot request, create or settle clearance.
  3. System updates the clearance status and closes it on settlement.
Exception Conditions
Exceptions
  • If no accountable student is recorded on the borrowing slip, the system refuses to raise the clearance until the responsible student is identified on the source record.
  • If a clearance remains unsettled at the end of the term, it stays open in Clearance Records. Outstanding clearances are not included in the Lab End-Term Report.

Related Use CasesProcess Return, Manage Equipment Inventory
Stakeholders
Stakeholder Interests

Conditions
Preconditions
  • The item or waste is physically present and traceable to inventory or a borrowing return outcome.
  • The user is signed in.
Postconditions

ActorSystem

  1. System displays eligible inventory and return outcomes; the Broken, Loss and Consumed log is a view of these records, not an additional DFD store.

Exceptions

Table 22Generate End-Term Report
Use Case NameGenerate End-Term Report
ScenarioHead Laboratory reviews recorded usage for a selected term in the Physics Laboratory Logs or Circuits Laboratory Logs reporting view.
Triggering EventHead Laboratory selects the laboratory and term and generates the Lab End-Term Report.
Brief DescriptionFor each laboratory separately, the system derives three summary tables from reservation-linked usage logs, borrowing/item transactions and inventory quantities: Average Equipment Use, Top 5 Equipment & Consumables, and Laboratory Frequency Usage. Recent Activity supplies the supporting transaction log. These are deterministic, non-AI calculations. Disposal, non-transaction daily tasks, and outstanding clearances are excluded; there is no appendix for those records.
ActorsHead Laboratory
Related Use CasesIssue Equipment, Process Return, Manage Logs, Schedule & Daily Tasks
Stakeholders
Stakeholder Interests
  • Head Laboratory: needs source-traceable item-use summaries and session-frequency figures for each laboratory without manually maintaining spreadsheet formulas.
  • NU Fairview administration: receives the figures required at the end of each term.
Conditions
Preconditions
  • The laboratory and term are selected, and the relevant reservation, session, borrowing and inventory records are accessible.
  • Head Laboratory is signed in.
Postconditions
  • The selected laboratory's report contains the three named summary tables and Recent Activity; Physics and Circuits data are not mixed. Every figure is traceable to source records and the report can be exported by Head Laboratory.
Flow of Activities
ActorSystem
  1. Head Laboratory opens Physics Laboratory Logs or Circuits Laboratory Logs for Lab End-Term reporting.
  2. Head Laboratory selects the term and reviews the three summary tables and Recent Activity.
  3. Head Laboratory exports the report for submission.
  1. System filters source records by the selected laboratory and term. Reservation records identify the session and requester; actual usage and item transactions establish recorded use. A reservation that never took place is not counted as laboratory use.
  2. System builds Average Equipment Use with Item, Quantity Used, Total Available, Avg Use %, and Top Requester. Avg Use % = ROUND(Quantity Used / Total Available * 100, 2). The legacy spreadsheet's $O$5 text concatenation is only a display label, not part of the percentage calculation. Total Available must have a traceable inventory basis for the report period; do not silently substitute another denominator or cap repeated-use ratios at 100%.
  3. System builds Top 5 Equipment & Consumables by ranking items by recorded Total Used within the same laboratory and term, showing Rank, Item, and Total Used. Consumables remain identified by their item type; Consumed is retained separately in the supporting log.
  4. System builds Laboratory Frequency Usage with Professor / Requester, Times Used, and Usage %. Times Used counts actual laboratory sessions, not hours or item rows. Usage % = ROUND(requester session count / total session count * 100, 2). Count each session once even when it has several item rows. For 4 and 5 sessions, the total is 9 and the shares are 44.44% and 55.56%.
  5. System displays Recent Activity with Date, Laboratory / class reference, Professor / Requester, Item, Qty, Consumed, and Type. The report has no disposal, daily-task or outstanding-clearance appendix. Head Laboratory can export the same three summary tables and supporting log.
Exception Conditions
Exceptions
  • If no sessions exist, display an empty report with zero session totals and no fabricated rankings. An undefined percentage, including a zero or missing denominator, is displayed as N/A rather than Infinity or a misleading percentage.
  • If source records are incomplete or the report-period inventory denominator cannot be established, identify the missing data; do not invent counts, percentages or Top Requester values.
  • If the export fails, Head Laboratory is notified and may retry.

3.1.5Gap Analysis

#

Table 23 groups the current-system gaps and proposed changes. These groups are not a one-to-one numbering of the product backlog; recurrence remains a consultation item. The Analytics page provides the explicit backlog-to-use-case and DFD traceability matrix.

Table 23: Gap Analysis

IDCurrent SystemProposed ChangesImpact
01Inventory is held in the inventory finder worksheet as name, description, existing quantity, unit and type, with no condition field and no record of how much of each item is currently out or committed; edits are typed directly into cells.Provide an inventory module supporting add, edit and remove, in which each holding is recorded by name with a condition status and quantities tracked as existing, available, in use and reserved.Stock levels become visible at a glance and changes are attributable rather than silently overwritten.
02Borrowing is recorded in the Physics and Circuits usage logs by date, subject code, professor, particulars and quantity; no student is named anywhere in the workbook.Provide a Borrowing Slip Record capturing the requester, applicable participating students (selected group members or the selected individual student), issued items, quantities, date, and time against the approved reservation.Accountability attaches to the borrower rather than only to the supervising professor.
03Damage and loss are logged by date, professor, item, quantity and unit; the accountable group is traceable only through the signed paper slip for that session.Record damage and loss against the borrowing transaction; Head Laboratory identifies the responsible student from its Group or Student Only participants before raising clearance.Removes the paper cross-reference step and prevents unattributed losses.
04Availability is established by opening the inventory finder and reading a quantity that is updated by hand after each session.Provide a live availability view showing quantities on hand and expected return times.Availability can be checked without a physical count.
05End-of-term figures are computed by formula blocks in the Broken, Loss and Consumed worksheet and exported manually into a presentation.Generate summaries and transaction logs directly from stored records.Reporting no longer depends on preserving a hand-built formula set.
06Clearance is issued on paper, signed by the student, a faculty member and the laboratory head, then forwarded to the registrar.Provide a digital clearance record raised and tracked by the laboratory head.Removes lost and incomplete clearance records and shortens processing time.

10Out-of-schedule use is arranged in person or by email against vacant blocks. 3.1.6Context Diagram

#

Figure 2 presents the system as one process at DFD Level 0. Its six external entities match the Use Case Diagram and each appears once. The Class Representative and Faculty exchange request, availability, status, history, question-and-answer, and Borrowing Slip data within their permitted workflows; only the Class Representative receives Clearance Status. The Dean remains approval-only. Head Laboratory exchanges account, inventory, equipment, clearance, schedule, usage, daily-task, disposal, and reporting data across both laboratories. Physics and Circuits Laboratory Staff exchange inventory, equipment, and disposal data only for their assigned laboratory; they do not send schedule, usage-log, clearance, or daily-task actions. These 46 boundary flows are preserved in the Level 1 DFD. Laboratory dashboards remain read-only views of existing records; their presentation arrows are intentionally omitted from these DFDs.

3.1.7Data Flow Diagrams

#

Level 1

#

Figure 3 is the formal detailed reference: it decomposes the system into five primary processes and ten canonical data stores, retaining the individual boundary flows. Process 1.0 manages user access and controlled account issuance. Process 2.0 manages reservations, availability, approvals, status, and history. Process 3.0 answers authenticated laboratory questions. Process 4.0 manages inventory, equipment issuance and return, Borrowing Slip Records, disposal, and optional Head Lab inventory forecasting. Process 5.0 manages schedules, session usage, Head-Laboratory-controlled daily tasks and clearance, and end-term reporting. Only Head Laboratory sends Schedule Update, Usage Entry, Daily Task Entry, and Clearance Action. Laboratory Staff contribute inventory, issuance/return, and disposal records within their assigned laboratory. The 73 independent flows comprise 48 external exchanges and 25 store exchanges. Forecast Request and Inventory Forecast are Head Lab boundary exchanges; historical item references support dynamic forecasting. Dashboard presentation arrows are omitted without removing the dashboard feature. Head Laboratory appears last in the entity column.

Level 2

#

Figures 4 to 8 decompose the five-process formal Level 1 model into five separate images. Each uses the same plain, print-oriented style as Level 1: uniform peer shapes, a vertical child-process column, independent noun-labelled arrows, and clear space beneath each label. Every Level 1 boundary flow is mapped to its child process; separate reads and writes may realize the same parent flow at different stages. Full names and parent-flow references remain available in the editable diagram. Borrowing Slip, Clearance, Daily Task, and Disposal Records remain distinct. Only Head Laboratory manages Daily Tasks, and Process 3.0 remains an informational Q&A chatbot.

Open canonical DFD Level 2 diagrams

DFD Levels 0–2 use the same concise data-flow labels for both requesting roles: On-Schedule Request and Out-of-Schedule Request. For Faculty, On-Schedule Request means the laboratory activity within the assigned class schedule; it needs no additional academic approval. For Class Representatives, the on-schedule non-laboratory request requires the selected class Faculty's approval. Process 2.3 routes a Class Representative out-of-schedule request to Faculty then Dean when the assigned Faculty is available; it may route directly to Dean only when that Faculty is unavailable. Faculty out-of-schedule requests go directly to Dean. Group / Student Only applies only to Class Representatives. Any rejection stops routing and releases the hold.

Process 2.4 retains Pending (awaiting Dean) and the held block after intermediate Faculty approval or the documented Faculty-unavailability direct route; only the final required approval sets Approved. Pending Dean is a reviewer stage, not a new reservation-status value. Process 4.2 retrieves only finally approved reservations for issuance; Pending requests cannot proceed to Process 4.3. Existing Faculty/Dean, D2 approval-record and authorized-reservation flows carry these rules without additional arrows.

3.1.8Entity-Relationship Diagram

#

Logical ERD draft — pending consultation and validation. One complete black-and-white A4 portrait diagram maps all ten canonical DFD stores to 25 entities and 51 primary-key/foreign-key relationships. Each table appears once. Crow’s Foot connectors attach to the key rows, while the data dictionary records optional relationships, uniqueness and workflow constraints.

Inventory Forecasting reads ITEM / inventory records, BORROWING, BORROWING_ITEM and RETURN_ENTRY, resolving each item through REQUEST_ITEM. Consumption uses RETURN_ENTRY.qty_consumed; reusable-equipment demand uses issue and partial-return timing, not summed borrow counts. Dynamic results require no new table, key or relationship. Forecast generation does not write inventory. Reservation revisions, recurrence, room-only completion, clearance completion, atomic stock holds and knowledge-base ownership retain their existing consultation status. The archived ERD and email approval tokens remain excluded.

RESERVATION.reservation_type records GROUP or STUDENT_ONLY and is required for every Class Representative reservation. Schedule Type remains separate in REQUEST_REVISION.request_basis / usage_type. One active representative account per section can link to multiple CLASS_GROUP subject/class records. The requester selects an authorized active class; its faculty_id determines the Faculty reviewer, not the Faculty who delivered the account credentials. The backend must enforce section representative uniqueness across active class assignments and validate the chosen class, term, section and schedule together. REQUEST_MEMBER retains members of the selected class or records the one selected student for Student Only. RESERVATION.requester_id identifies the submitting Class Rep separately from the participating students. Faculty requests retain their existing workflow.
